question: Can rare-variant information be evaluated incrementally over the frozen chr22 Gnomix baseline without donor leakage or representation drift?

gates.name: artifact_and_coordinate_contract
gates.pass_rule: Inputs are hashable, chr22/hg38-compatible, biallelic and ordered; model C equals the frozen reference marker count; genetic positions are monotonic.

gates.name: donor_identity_independence_and_parentals
gates.pass_rule: Baseline donors and relatives can be excluded, ambiguous identities are fingerprinted, and each ancestry has locus-defensible donor units.

gates.name: frozen_baseline_marker_compatibility
gates.pass_rule: The external donor panel contains at least 80 percent of exact model markers without ad hoc imputation, padding, liftover or retraining.

gates.name: fit_only_wgs_rare_support_and_phase
gates.pass_rule: After family-disjoint splitting, FIT-only minor alleles have MAC at least 2, MAF below 1 percent, at least two independent carrier units and auditable haplotype phase.

gates.name: identifiability_and_power_envelope
gates.pass_rule: Independent donor capacity, cM coverage and an externally chosen SESOI permit a preregistered TRAIN/VALIDATION pilot without opening TEST.

future_estimand.comparison: same L2 multinomial corrector with baseline-only features versus baseline plus rare features
future_estimand.primary: paired absolute reduction in position-wise ancestry-dose error, macro-averaged across ancestries
future_estimand.uncertainty: paired bootstrap over complete donor packages

stop_rules: Stop before simulation if any of G0, G1 or G2 fails.
Do not use DNABR rare VCFs, Gnomix predictions or NAMBR labels as independent locus truth.
Do not fill absent baseline markers as 0/0 or by an unregistered imputation or substitution step.
Do not select rare variants, windows, generations, sample size or SESOI using TEST performance.
A negative result from a marker-ascertained panel does not refute the WGS rare-variant hypothesis.
